I've been working on my personal statement for weeks and I still don't love it. I grew up in a small town where most people never left, and I always felt like I wanted to see more of the world. When I was fifteen I started volunteering at the local library, teaching older adults how to use computers. One woman, Mrs. Alvarez, wanted to video call her grandkids in another country. It took us six weeks, but the first time she saw their faces on the screen, she cried, and so did I. That moment showed me that technology is only as good as the people it helps. Since then, I've taught coding to kids, built a small app for our food pantry, and started studying computer science. I want to keep building things that make people feel closer, not further apart. In college, I hope to study human-computer interaction and keep finding ways to make technology kinder.
